paragraphs: On Thursday after lunch, Coach Matt met the Explorers on the school field. He had a big bag, a silver whistle, and two blue sheets. "Today we play the Tent Game," he said. "It is good practice for camping." "Is it a race?" asked Leo. "Yes, but first you must listen to the rules," said Coach Matt. "I will say each step slowly, and you can ask questions."

"Make two teams of two," said Coach Matt. Lily and Leo made one team, and Mia and May made the other team. "Each team gets one sheet, one rope, and four stones," he said. "Each team also gets a notebook." Four poles were already in the ground, two for each team. Coach Matt gave the bags to the teams, and everybody looked at him.

"There are five steps, including the last step with the notebook," he said. "Step one, tie the rope between the two poles, and pull it hard." "Step two, put the sheet over the rope." "The sheet must go down on both sides." "Step three, put one stone on each corner of the sheet." "The stones hold the tent on the ground." "Step four, make the ground flat inside the tent." "Step five, both players sit inside and put a hand up." "I will say the time, and one player writes it in the notebook."

"Now the rules," said Coach Matt. "You cannot start before the whistle." "You cannot throw the stones, and you cannot move the poles." "Keep in contact with your partner, and talk all the time." "For example, say, 'I have the rope, so you take the sheet.'" "Can we start now?" asked May. "Wait for one more moment," said Coach Matt with a smile. "Are there any questions?" Nobody spoke, so he lifted the whistle to his mouth.

Coach Matt used the whistle, and the two teams ran to their poles. "I have the rope!" called Lily. "Then I take the sheet," said Leo. At the other poles, Mia put one stone on a corner of the sheet. "Your corner is not flat," said May. Both teams worked fast, and nobody threw a stone. Soon four players sat inside two small tents with their hands up. "Good work, both teams," said Coach Matt. Mia wrote the time in the notebook, and Leo laughed very loudly. "The tent is simple," said Coach Matt, "but a good plan makes it easy."
